correctness.rationale: All four neighbors are distinct for m,n≥3, so the indicator problem is exactly Ax=1 over F₂, with A=S+S⁻¹+T+T⁻¹. An independent short route to the decisive identity verifies the polynomial proof: U=ST and V=ST⁻¹ commute and (I+U)(I+V)=SA. If Ax=1, multiply the resulting (I+U)(I+V)x=1 by the two length-a geometric sums in U and V. Each sum fixes the constant-one vector because a is odd. Thus (I+Uᵃ)(I+Vᵃ)x=1. When m divides 2a, I+S²ᵃ cancels in this product, so Sᵃ(Tᵃ+T⁻ᵃ)x=1, or (I+T²ᵃ)x=1. This verifies the asserted shift and normalization for every feasible solution. If 4 divides neither dimension, the order of T²ᵃ is n/gcd(n,2a), odd; iteration is impossible. In the mixed case the shift pairs selected and unselected sites and gives exactly mn/2. The column-only 0011 series is feasible when 4 divides n; the two neighbors in the fixed coordinate agree, while those in the varying coordinate have opposite membership. When both lengths are fourfold, incidences give |D|≥mn/4. In the period-4 witness rows 0 and 2 contain complementary adjacent column pairs, rows 1 and 3 are empty, each vertex in an occupied row sees one horizontal selected neighbor, and each in an empty row sees one vertical selected neighbor. The pattern therefore attains equality, including length 4; swapping coordinates proves the other asymmetric case.
residual_risks: The documented Gaussian elimination covers 196 size pairs, and exhaustive Gray-code support minimization covers eight small tori. Neither is used to extrapolate; uploaded code was not executed.
Uses binary parity in the simple four-neighbor Cartesian graph, not closed-neighborhood parity or degenerate length-two factors.

evidence: Goldwasser–Klostermeyer's available abstract describes odd/even open domination on m×n grids, while Yamagishi's abstract concerns periodic harmonic function dimensions.

Dejter's primary Corollary 6 and Kraner Šumenjak et al.'s Theorem 2.2 concern parallel exact-one codes on cycle products. The latter paper distinguishes the general EOD characterization as Conjecture 2.4.
Hu–Xu's toroidal total domination problem requires at least one selected neighbor rather than an odd number.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Finite path-grid boundaries cannot simply be replaced by toroidal ones. The exact-one results already imply the fourfold positive branch, and even a theorem excluding all exact-one codes in mixed tori would not imply parity feasibility or force the weights of all odd-open solutions. Ordinary total domination and homogeneous nullity are related but distinct problems.

evidence: An exact-one code is an odd-open solution with weight mn/4 by incidence, so the published fourfold existence theorem mechanically settles that minimum in the fourfold-by-fourfold regime.

Symmetry over F₂ gives solvability iff every homogeneous null vector has even coordinate sum, but nullity alone provides no such sum test. Temporal Jordan claims inspected concern restricted parameters, not the arbitrary odd-factor translation condition.
The audited antiperiodicity implies nonexistence of any efficient open set in mixed tori as a consequence, since every odd-open solution there is too large.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Credit known quarter density and standard linear-algebra reductions. The actual affine shift identity gives both the odd-order obstruction and the half-weight rigidity; neither follows from the inspected efficient-open existence theorem or from an abstract dimension computation.

Closed-neighborhood toggling is not equivalent. Knowing dim ker A determines image dimension but not whether the specific all-ones vector lies in it or the support of its inverse images.

originality.rationale: The full odd-open phase diagram and forced complementation are the distinct claims supported by the comparison. The both-fourfold quarter-density branch by itself is covered: prior existence of parallel total perfect codes gives equality in the four-regular incidence bound. No originality credit is assigned to that branch in isolation. Perfect open domination results do not settle the affine parity problem in the other regimes, where the number of selected neighbors may be three.
residual_risks: The Goldwasser–Klostermeyer and Yamagishi full texts could not be inspected at their decisive theorem pages. The available material is not proof that they omit a toroidal affine theorem.

The later status of the unrestricted EOD conjecture was not established and may affect how much of the exact-one consequence is new, not by itself the odd-open phase diagram. Equivalent neighbor-only toggling or periodic binary lattice work beyond this bounded search remains a priority risk.

value.rationale: Feasibility, exact support, and a constraint on every configuration on a standard periodic graph are useful beyond the known perfect-code case. The odd factor of a circumference forces a translation to exchange selected and unselected sites, explaining why the mixed regime cannot approach domination density one quarter and why the other regime is empty. This is a structural classification, not a re-computation of the fourfold code or a small finite census.
residual_risks: No count or complete weight distribution is claimed outside the rigid half-density branch, and no application to other neighborhoods is proved.
